newsitem.title: JAPAN: Stable currencies desirable--Japan EPA's Nukaya.
newsitem.headline: Stable currencies desirable--Japan EPA's Nukaya.

text.p: Japan's Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Vice Minister Shimpei Nukaya said on Friday it was desirable for currencies to move in a stable manner.
He said currency movements are too rapid when the yen moves against the dollar by nearly one yen or more per day and heads in the same direction at that pace for two to three days or more.
"It is desirable for them (currencies) to move in a stable manner," Nukaya said at a regular news conference.
He added that it is possible for the yen to head in a certain direction over a long period of time, but it is not desirable for it to move too much in one direction in a short period of time.
He said recent yen movements seemed to have been influenced by Japanese buying of foreign bonds due to the interest rate gap between Japan and the United States.
"But the movement this past few days has been very rapid," Nukaya said.
Asked for his view of the yen's movements on Friday, Nukaya said it did not seem to be moving very much and had recovered a bit against the dollar.
